function: Estimation of the direct and cascaded channels H=[d, G] of a RIS-aided mmWave SIMO uplink from noisy pilots, with an attention-based denoising encoder-decoder (pp. 2-3).
system: RIS-aided SIMO uplink at mmWave (band not stated); passive reflecting RIS, N=32 elements (UPA); BS ULA with M=16 antennas; one-antenna UE; L=33 pilots (pp. 2, 4).
method: CNN encoder-decoder with multi-view attention blocks (K=3 extractors, C=96); supervised offline training on NMSE of channel and noise-free signal; only encoder online (pp. 3-4).
data_channel: Custom simulation: Saleh-Valenzuela mmWave channels with P1=P2=3, P3=2 paths, random AoA/AoD, CSCG gains; 96000 training samples, 4000 test samples per SNR (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: Training at SNR -10 to 15 dB, testing at each SNR level in the same range, same M=16, N=32, L=33 and channel model; no unseen scenario (p. 4).
baselines: Non-learned: LS, LMMSE [15]; learned: CNN [16], SC-attention [10], CDRN [11]; also ablation variants of the proposed network (pp. 4-5).
metrics: NMSE of direct and cascaded channels versus SNR (Figs. 4-5, pp. 4-5); online MACs and parameters (Table I, p. 5).
complexity: Table I: online MACs of 35.63 G/s and 1.08 M parameters for the proposed network, against 10.06 to 471.27 G/s for the learned baselines (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 2: "The mmWave channels are based on the Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) model [8]"; a custom simulator, and no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO, COST 2100 or measured channel is used.
q2_support: p. 4: "At each SNR level, the number of samples for online estimation is I = 4000"; training and testing share M, N, L and the channel model, and only the SNR varies; no unseen scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 5: "compares it with the LS estimator, LMMSE estimator [15], CNN [16], SC-attention [10], and CDRN [11]"
q4_support: p. 5: "Table I compares the online model parameters and online computational complexity multiply-accumulates (MACs) of all DL-based baselines"; the table also lists the proposed network.
q5_support: p. 2: "The mmWave channels are based on the Saleh-Valenzuela (SV) model [8]"; the channels are simulated, and no link, DOI, release statement, public dataset or measured data appears in the paper.
notes: Included as area 2: the learned encoder estimates the direct and cascaded channel matrix H=[d, G] from noisy pilots (pp. 2-3). Fig. 4 compares ablation variants of the proposed network (p. 4), which do not count as learned baselines; q3 rests on LS and LMMSE (non-learned) and on CNN [16], SC-attention [10] and CDRN [11] (learned) in Fig. 5 (p. 5), all on NMSE. q4 rests on Table I (p. 5). q1 is 0 because the Saleh-Valenzuela model is a custom simulator. q2 is 0 because only the SNR changes between training and testing (p. 4).
